text:
maya_cust: hey @support — our batch rerank call is returning scores that don't match the per-query candidate lists. the scores look shifted: query B is getting scores that belong to query A. noticed after upgrading to the new /v2/rerank batch endpoint. request id 8f1a2d.

morgan: sorry about that, can you paste a minimal repro payload and the response you got? also is this happening for all jobs or only some customers?

maya_cust: happening for a handful of customers, started yesterday after we switched to batching. minimal payload below (redacted):
```json
{
  "requests": [
    {"query": "What is the refund policy?", "candidates": ["30 days back", "No refunds"]},
    {"query": "How to change billing?", "candidates": []},
    {"query": "Cancel subscription", "candidates": ["cancel page", "support contact"]}
  ]
}
```
response snippet: 
```json
{
  "results": [
    {"scores": [0.12, 0.03]},
    {"scores": []},
    {"scores": [0.74, 0.66]}
  ]
}
```
but the user-saw mapping was wrong — the middle empty candidate query got omitted in our UI and the third query's scores were shown for the second question. also some customers reported unexpected NaN/inf values once.

jia: thanks — that payload is super helpful. suspecting an off-by-one in the prefix-sum offsets when we build the flattened candidate buffer, specifically when a per-query candidates length = 0. packing code currently does a compaction step that drops zero-length segments and then applies offsets without keeping placeholders. i'll try to repro locally. can you also send the original raw http logs (request headers + request body + X-Request-Id)?

maya_cust: sending logs via DM. also one more thing: we started seeing billing hits for these bad rerank calls (charged per-candidate) — not ideal.

morgan: copying @billing to this thread. we'll issue a credit while we investigate. please send the earliest failing request ids and account id.

carlos: pinging in case this is related to the batching optimizer that does candidate deduping. if we dedupe across queries and then collapse indexes, that could cause misalignment if we don't re-expand with empty slots. i'll look at the batching layer.

jia: quick repro confirm: ran the exact payload against a local dev server and reproduced the offset shift. the flattened indices ended up [0,2,2,4] instead of [0,2,2,4] — wait that's the same numbers but we dropped a placeholder so decode mapped the third pair to the second query. stacktrace points to rerank/packer.py:build_flat_buffer -> compact_candidates(). adding a test for zero-length candidate lists now.

morgan: good triage. what's the immediate mitigation? return 400 if any request has an empty candidates array? we probably can't force customers to change payloads.

jia: i pushed a guard to validation that ensures candidates arrays are present (allowing empty) but the server must leave placeholder offsets for empty lists. deploying a hotfix to staging now, will backport to canary + prod if tests pass.

rerank-bot: deploy started for branch fix/retain-empty-candidate-offsets to canary (deploy id deploy-2026-03-15-19).

morgan: once canary is up, i'll ask the affected customers to test. also billing: i've created credits for accounts A-341 and B-112 and flagged other affected invoices pending review.

maya_cust: thanks — can you also add a response field that echoes per-query candidate_counts so our UI can validate mapping? that would help detect regressions on our side.

jia: yeah we can add an optional header X-Per-Query-Counts in responses for a while (list of integers) — i'll add it to the canary so you can opt in.

carlos: follow-ups: add an integration test that exercises "mixed empty + non-empty candidate lists" across multiple batch sizes, and add a fuzzer to try random empty placements. also audit the dedupe/compact logic.

morgan: recording action items -> ENG: add validation + preserve offsets (jia), add tests & fuzzer (carlos). SUPPORT: notify affected customers and issue credits (morgan). BILLING: review charges (morgan).

maya_cust: confirmed canary test passed for our sample payload, thanks! when will prod roll be expected?

jia: aiming for prod rollout in ~2 hours after warmup and perf checks. will post update.

morgan: thanks everyone — tagging this as resolved once prod deploy is healthy. will follow up with postmortem summary and the customer communications. :thumbsup:
